items.case_name: Bayer/Monsanto Roundup $7.25B Class Settlement — Fairness Hearing
items.parties: Roundup Cancer Claimants v. Monsanto Company (Bayer AG)
items.court: 22nd Judicial Circuit Court, St. Louis, Missouri
items.why: The fairness hearing for this $7.25B claims-made settlement (preliminary approval March 4, 2026) was rescheduled to August 19, 2026 — squarely within the last 10 days' horizon. The opt-out period closed June 4, 2026, so denominator math is now set; Monsanto retains a termination right if opt-outs exceed a threshold. Per-claim recoveries range from $6,000–$198,000+ for NHL diagnoses, and claims open only after final approval, creating a post-approval filing-rate arbitrage opportunity.

items.case_name: In re PG&E Corp. Securities Litigation ($100M Settlement — Final Approval Aug 25)
items.parties: Public Employees' Retirement Association of New Mexico (PERA) et al. v. PG&E Corporation et al.
items.why: The July 6, 2026 objection deadline passed with zero objections filed, eliminating appellate overhang risk; the final approval hearing is set for August 25, 2026. The $100M fund (fully D&O-insurance-funded per the 10-Q) is a clean claims-made PSLRA settlement with a compressed distribution timeline — zero-objector posture means distribution timing is highly predictable, making per-share recovery math reliable for this desk's valuation of tradeable claims.

items.case_name: In re YSA (Lending Firm)
items.parties: YSA (debtor); creditors holding $500M+ in claims
items.why: A lending firm identified as 'YSA' filed Chapter 11 on or about July 29, 2026 with over $500M in debt, surfacing in the Law360 large-cap docket feed — one of the largest financials-sector free-falls of the week and consistent with the record 2026 surge in financials Chapter 11s in the $100M–$500M band. The creditor recovery angle, DIP financing structure, and classification of loan-book assets are all live issues worth monitoring at first-day.

items.case_name: Holland & Knight CAPE Phase 3 / Finally-Liquidated CIT Orders (July 15 batch)
items.parties: ~3,700 individual IEEPA plaintiff-importers v. United States (consolidated before Judge Eaton, CIT)
items.why: On July 15, 2026 the CIT entered an order directing CBP to refund IEEPA duties on a plaintiff's finally-liquidated entries and signaled it will issue substantially identical orders in all ~3,700 pending IEEPA cases; the court confirmed that importers who have NOT filed suit have no comparable, confirmed refund mechanism for finally-liquidated entries. This directly prices the gap between plaintiff and non-plaintiff refund receivables — a core valuation input for any claims-purchase thesis.

items.case_name: Hachette et al. v. Google LLC (Gemini)
items.parties: Hachette Book Group, Inc.; Cengage Learning, Inc.; Elsevier Inc.; Scott Turow; S.C.R.I.B.E. v. Google LLC
items.why: Filed July 10, 2026 — three major publishers plus Scott Turow allege Google trained Gemini on millions of copyrighted books licensed only for Google Books snippets, with willful stripping of copyright-management information; the class seeks statutory damages and destruction of unauthorized training copies, making this the highest-profile new plaintiff-side recovery vehicle since Bartz and a direct comparator for per-work damages valuation across the AI-copyright system.

items.case_name: NYT v. OpenAI (MDL No. 3143) — Sanctions Motion
items.parties: The New York Times Co. et al. (17-publisher coalition) v. OpenAI, Inc.; Microsoft Corporation — In re OpenAI, Inc. Copyright Infringement Litigation, MDL No. 1:25-md-03143
items.why: A coalition of 17 news organizations filed a sweeping sanctions motion in late June/early July 2026 accusing OpenAI of running internal copyright-violation searches it claimed were impossible and simultaneously deleting billions of court-ordered ChatGPT conversation logs; if granted, the sanction could hand publishers a trial-altering evidentiary win without requiring merits proof, dramatically accelerating the settlement-pressure and recovery timeline for this $-billion-plus exposure MDL.

items.case_name: DOJ Federal Circuit Appeal of CIT Universal IEEPA Refund Order (Atmus / Euro-Notions line)
items.parties: United States v. Atmus Filtration, Inc. et al. / Euro-Notions Florida LLC et al.
items.court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
items.why: DOJ filed its notice of appeal on June 2–3, 2026, arguing the CIT's universal refund order is an impermissible injunction and that finally-liquidated non-plaintiff entries require importer-specific court orders; the Federal Circuit has the case, and a stay ruling would freeze CAPE Phase 3 payouts for non-litigants. The desk must track this appeal because an adverse ruling could bifurcate the refund universe, crashing the value of non-plaintiff receivables while lifting plaintiff claims.

items.case_name: Kadrey v. Meta — Contributory Infringement Amendment
items.parties: Richard Kadrey et al. v. Meta Platforms, Inc.
items.why: On December 11, 2025 (the leading pleading event now ripening into 2026 motion practice), authors moved to amend to add a contributory-infringement claim over Meta's alleged 'seeding' of pirated book torrents to third parties — the surviving exposure after Meta won fair-use on training itself; this seeding theory is the litigation's live damages vector and directly cross-references the Bartz piracy-acquisition framework as the standard for non-fair-use liability.
